description: One SEO element repaired or improved per iteration, evidence-first: every story is verified against the actual prerendered output in website/dist/client, not against intent. Work that does not fit a single iteration is written down here rather than half-attempted. Strategy context lives in pSEO.md and docs/SEO_STRATEGY.md.

userStories.title: Unbreak the website production build so SEO changes can actually deploy
userStories.description: As the site owner, I want `npm run build` to succeed so that Cloudflare Pages keeps deploying, because every SEO surface this repo owns (prerendered HTML, canonicals, JSON-LD, sitemap.xml, the IndexNow ping) is emitted by that one script.
acceptanceCriteria: `npx tsc -b` exits 0 in website/
`npm run build` exits 0 and prerenders every route
dist/client/sitemap.xml is regenerated and non-empty
A GitHub Actions workflow gates website/** pull requests on the build
userStories.notes: Root cause: src/test/fonts.test.ts (added by US-WEB020) uses node:fs and __dirname, but tsconfig.app.json includes src/ with types ['vite/client'] only, so tsc -b exited 2 and the whole build script stopped before vite build. Fixed by giving the tests their own project (tsconfig.test.json) and excluding src/test from the app project. Guarded by .github/workflows/website-check.yml.

userStories.title: Make website eslint clean and add it to the CI gate
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want `npm run lint` green and gated so that the website check workflow can enforce it the way edge-functions-check.yml enforces deno lint.
acceptanceCriteria: `npm run lint` exits 0 in website/
No rule is disabled wholesale to get there — each error is fixed or suppressed inline with a reason
A `Lint` step is added back to .github/workflows/website-check.yml and passes
userStories.notes: 9 errors / 10 warnings today, concentrated in react-hooks/set-state-in-effect (Blog.tsx, BlogPost.tsx, admin/*) and @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any (utils/analytics.ts). The set-state-in-effect ones are real refactors of the blog data-loading path, not cosmetic — likely its own iteration.

userStories.title: Stop leaking a JSX comment block into every page's <head>
userStories.description: As a crawler, I want the document head to contain only markup so that the shipped HTML is valid and not padded with source commentary.
acceptanceCriteria: No `{/*` sequence appears in any file under dist/client
The explanatory prose survives as a real source comment in pages/+onRenderHtml.tsx or as an HTML comment
fonts.test.ts still passes
userStories.notes: Root cause: STATIC_HEAD in pages/+onRenderHtml.tsx is a template literal in a .tsx file, so the JSX comment written inside it was copied byte-for-byte into the head of all 34 prerendered documents (940 bytes each, 31960 total). The prose now lives in a real TypeScript comment above the literal. Guarded twice: src/test/head.test.ts asserts the literal carries no JSX comment syntax, and website-check.yml greps the emitted dist/client HTML, which is what crawlers actually read.

userStories.title: Remove or configure the placeholder Cloudflare Insights beacon
userStories.description: As a visitor, I don't want a third-party script requested on every page with a token that was never filled in, because it costs a connection on the LCP path and returns nothing.
acceptanceCriteria: No script tag ships with a literal PLACEHOLDER/YOUR_* token
Either a real token is injected from an env var at build time, or the beacon is removed
If it stays, it is gated behind the same consent flow as GA4 (src/lib/consent.ts)
userStories.notes: The tag now renders only when VITE_CF_ANALYTICS_TOKEN holds a 32-hex token, and the token is validated before interpolation because it lands inside a JSON attribute. Verified across three builds: no token -> 0 beacons, real token -> 34 beacons with the token intact, hostile token -> 0 beacons plus a build warning. OWNER ACTION: /privacy and /cookies tell visitors Cloudflare Web Analytics is in use; that is only true once the token is set in the Cloudflare Pages build environment.

userStories.title: Complete the social card contract across every page family
userStories.description: As a link shared into Slack/X/iMessage, I want a fully-specified card so previews render large instead of falling back to a small thumbnail while the image is fetched.
acceptanceCriteria: og:image:width, og:image:height and og:image:type emitted alongside og:image
Dimensions match the real og-image.png rather than being assumed
SEO.tsx accepts an optional per-page image so comparison and /what-to-do pages can override the sitewide default
userStories.notes: Bigger than the original note. Two page families — the 10 comparison pages and every blog post — hand-rolled their own <Helmet> and emitted NO og:image and NO twitter:card at all, so the highest commercial-intent URLs on the site shared as bare links. Both now go through <SEO>, which also gained og:image:width/height/type (measured from the real PNG and asserted against its IHDR), og:locale, article timestamps, a per-page image override, an explicit-canonical override, and `<` escaping in the JSON-LD payload that BlogPost previously had and the shared component did not. Verified in dist: compare pages carry the full card, exactly one og:image / twitter:card / canonical / title per page, and all 59 emitted JSON-LD blocks parse.

userStories.title: Land the search-console verification tokens
userStories.description: As the site owner, I want Google, Bing and Yandex ownership verified so that indexing coverage and query data are observable at all.
acceptanceCriteria: Verification meta tags emitted from env vars, or ownership verified via DNS and the commented block deleted
No PASTE_* placeholder remains in pages/+onRenderHtml.tsx
userStories.notes: The three tags are commented out with PASTE_*_TOKEN placeholders. Real tokens are secrets and are not in this repo — this story needs values from the owner, so it is blocked on input rather than on effort.

userStories.title: Typecheck the pages/ directory
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want tsc to cover pages/ so that the file producing every page's <head> is not the one file nobody typechecks.
acceptanceCriteria: pages/**/*.ts(x) is included in a TypeScript project reachable from tsconfig.json
`npx tsc -b` exits 0 with it included
vike/types and vite/client types resolve there
userStories.notes: Added tsconfig.pages.json (types: node + vite/client, since the hooks run in Node but render browser markup and import .css) and referenced it from tsconfig.json. Only one pre-existing error surfaced — jsdom had no declarations in pages/fetchBlogForPrerender.ts — fixed by adding @types/jsdom as a devDependency rather than by declaring it any. Proved the gate bites: a planted `const x: number = 'a'` in +onRenderHtml.tsx fails tsc -b with TS2322. `npm run build` starts with tsc -b, so CI already gates it.

userStories.title: Stop Google truncating the comparison pages' SERP snippets
userStories.description: As a searcher comparing products, I want the result snippet to read as a complete thought so that the page's actual differentiator reaches me instead of being cut off mid-sentence.
acceptanceCriteria: Every comparison page title is <= 60 characters as rendered
Every comparison page description is <= 160 characters as rendered
Descriptions are hand-written for the SERP, not derived from page prose
A test fails if any competitor breaches either limit
userStories.notes: The description was `daily_ok_verdict.split('.').slice(0,2).join('.')` — the first two sentences of on-page prose, which has no length ceiling. Result: 225-407 characters on the ten highest commercial-intent URLs on the site, every one truncated. Added meta_description (and meta_title where needed) to the competitor JSON, and an appendBrand=false option to <SEO> because 'Daily OK vs. X … | Daily OK' spent 11 of ~60 characters saying the brand twice. Verified in dist: titles now 45-56, descriptions 139-157.

userStories.title: Bring the core and /what-to-do page snippets inside the rendered width
userStories.description: As a searcher, I want every page's snippet to read as a complete thought, not only the comparison pages fixed in US-SEO008.
acceptanceCriteria: Every indexable route's title is <= 60 characters as rendered (unescaped)
Every indexable route's description is <= 160 characters as rendered
The length assertion runs over the prerendered dist output, so it covers every page rather than one data file
The check is wired into .github/workflows/website-check.yml
userStories.notes: All 33 indexable routes now fit: titles 15-59 (was up to 79), descriptions 79-160 (was up to 266). 10 titles and 15 descriptions rewritten across 10 page components and src/data/whatToDo.ts. The check is now scripts/check-snippet-lengths.mjs, run in CI against the prerendered output: it measures UNESCAPED text (' is six characters in the file and one on screen), skips noindex routes, and warns rather than fails on /blog/* because that metadata is authored in the CMS. Proved it bites by planting a 340-character description in dist and watching it exit 1.

userStories.title: Stop starving the pSEO pages of internal links
userStories.description: As a crawler, I want the comparison and guide pages to be reachable from more than one place so that the pages the whole pSEO strategy rests on are not the least-linked URLs on the site.
acceptanceCriteria: Every comparison page receives the same number of sibling links
Every /what-to-do guide links sideways to sibling guides, not only up to the hub
Sibling selection is deterministic, so prerender and hydration agree
The sitewide link to the robots-disallowed /admin does not pass a follow signal
userStories.notes: ComparePost used competitors.filter(...).slice(0, 3) on a fixed-order array, so all ten pages pointed at the same first three: Life Alert 14 inbound, Life360 12, Snug Safety 11, and one each — from the hub — for the other six. The /what-to-do guides were worse: they linked up to the hub and sideways to nothing, one inbound link each against the hub's 32. rotatingSiblings() takes the next N entries after the current index with wraparound, so every item appears in exactly N sibling blocks regardless of array order. Measured in dist: comparison pages went from min 1 to min 4, guides from min 1 to min 4.

userStories.title: Generate llms.txt instead of hand-maintaining a stale one
userStories.description: As an AI crawler, I want the site's manifest to list every page that exists, at the URL that actually serves 200, so that the pages built for AI citation are the ones I can find.
acceptanceCriteria: llms.txt lists every indexable prerendered route
Every URL in llms.txt and llms-full.txt uses the trailing-slash form production serves
The file is generated at build time from the prerendered output, not hand-edited
CI fails if llms.txt and sitemap.xml disagree about which pages exist
userStories.notes: The hand-maintained file listed 18 of 33 routes. The 15 missing were the pSEO plan itself: seven of ten comparison pages, the whole /what-to-do cluster and /welfare-check-on-elderly-parent — and it carried a comment calling those guides 'not yet built' long after US-WEB005 built them. Every URL was in the no-slash form that production 308s (US-WEB010), so an agent that does not follow redirects got nothing. scripts/generate-llms-txt.mjs now walks the same prerendered output the sitemap walks and reads each page's own title and meta description, so blurbs cannot drift from the page. Blog posts are excluded on purpose: they publish between builds via the webhook, so a build-time list of them is wrong on arrival. Verified 33/33 routes, 0 redirecting URLs, and CI diffs llms.txt against sitemap.xml.

userStories.title: Give the content-hashed build output a real cache policy
userStories.description: As a returning visitor, I want the JS and CSS to come from my own cache so that the second page view is not gated on 1.4 MB of revalidation round-trips.
acceptanceCriteria: /assets/* is served with a one-year immutable Cache-Control
No stable-named path (HTML, sitemap.xml, robots.txt, llms.txt) is cached immutably
Unhashed brand assets get a bounded lifetime with stale-while-revalidate
A test asserts both directions, and that every unhashed public asset has a rule
userStories.notes: Cloudflare Pages sends `public, max-age=0, must-revalidate` for anything _headers does not mention, so the absence of a rule was a revalidation round-trip per navigation for every one of the content-hashed files under /assets. Only /fonts/* had a policy. The mirror-image mistake is worse and silent — an immutable year on a stable-named path pins visitors to a stale build — so the test pins both directions. Also added X-Robots-Tag: noindex to /admin, which _redirects rewrites to the homepage shell.

userStories.title: Confirm the CSP connect-src covers the Supabase host the blog fetches from
userStories.description: As a visitor reading a post published since the last deploy, I want the client-side fetch to succeed so that the post renders instead of an empty shell.
acceptanceCriteria: VITE_SUPABASE_URL's origin is present in the Content-Security-Policy connect-src
A post published via the generation webhook (no redeploy) renders in a browser with the production CSP applied
userStories.notes: BLOCKED ON INPUT, not effort. connect-src currently lists 'self', cloudflareinsights.com, api.dailyok.net, functions.dailyok.net and the Google Analytics hosts. src/lib/supabase.ts connects to VITE_SUPABASE_URL, whose production value is not in this repo. If Supabase is served from api.dailyok.net this is already fine and the story closes as a no-op; if it is a separate host (self-hosted Supabase usually is) then every client-side blog fetch and the admin login are CSP-blocked in production. Deliberately not guessed: adding a hostname that turns out to be wrong widens the policy for nothing and hides the real problem. Owner: confirm the value of VITE_SUPABASE_URL in the Cloudflare Pages build environment.
